dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing any code, read helpers.py, conftest.py, README, ALL 15 test files, and oracle_fixtures JSON — systematically extracting the concrete request/response shapes, discriminators, and payloads the client exercises.
Deliberate library selection (FastAPI/uvicorn/websockets/openpyxl) after checking installed packages — choosing OOXML I/O and server stack intentionally.

Re-consulted client behavior mid-build: discovered POST /api/workbooks must return sheets as a name list while GET returns full objects, inferred from what the smoke test asserts — contract-driven correction from observed client behavior.
Probed genuinely tricky Excel semantics rather than assuming: VLOOKUP range_lookup TRUE/FALSE, ISERROR exception capture, LET/LAMBDA named-function resolution vs parser uppercasing.

Grounded xlsx round-trip in openpyxl reality (named ranges/formats verified, _xlfn. prefix stripped) and corrected YEARFRAC basis and ROUND half-away semantics as new subsystems were reached — ongoing semantics verification, not just up-front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhaustively mapped the wire contract from helpers.py and the full smoke suite, chose libraries deliberately, verified openpyxl feature support, and repeatedly probed Excel semantics for the hard areas (spill, VLOOKUP, LET/LAMBDA, iterative, locale, xlsx round-trip) as it reached each subsystem — matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 10 because it never built a durable cross-referenced contract map, worked largely from memory, resolved ambiguities reactively rather than proactively, and did not independently consult a LibreOffice oracle beyond the given fixtures.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Explicit module-level decomposition plan (refs, parser, values, formats, locale, functions, engine, store, server, xlsx) with dependency-aware ordering — foundations before engine before server. This is genuine phasing, above a flat feature list.

Built the entire feature surface (all ~200 functions, engine, all endpoints, xlsx I/O) BEFORE launching the server or running any test; first test at step 54. Breadth-first rather than milestone-gated — fails the anchor-8 discriminator of getting a live server + core round-trip green before breadth.
Used the dev-test suite as per-stage done-check, tracking pass counts (78/80 → 83 → 131) and fixing bugs, showing checkpoints tied to runnable tests.

Systematic hardening phase with concrete risk-targeted done-checks: persistence-across-restart, perf probes (1000-chain, 5000-deps, 100k import), xlsx round-trip, locale persistence, SPA testid checklist — but applied as after-the-fact verification, not pre-declared gating milestones, and not revisited/re-ordered as a living plan.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent phases the work into sensible dependency-ordered stages (contract study → foundation modules → engine → server → validate → harden) with checkpoints per stage and a fairly rigorous risk-targeted hardening pass (perf, persistence, round-trip), which exceeds a flat to-do list (3) and matches the 'sensible stages with rough checkpoints' anchor (5) with extra verification substance. However it built the full breadth before ever launching/testing the server, so it lacks the anchor-8 discipline of getting a live server + persistence + core round-trip green before breadth, and its done-checks were the smoke suite plus post-hoc probes rather than a living, re-ordered milestone hierarchy. That places it at 6, between 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Ran dev_tests/run.sh repeatedly across suites; when engine tests failed (VLOOKUP exact-match #N/A, ISERROR sentinel) drilled into the specific failing cases with standalone python scripts and fixed them — failures driving fixes, not just green-run trust.

Built dedicated performance probes against the spec's stated ceilings: 1000-cell chain (~22ms), 5000-dependent propagation, 100k-cell import (~3s), and recompute timing — self-constructed perf verification beyond the smoke suite.
Wrote own openpyxl xlsx round-trip checks (named ranges + number formats) and CSV-with-formulas round-trip tests — round-trip oracles not in the visible suite.
Constructed persistence/restart verification (kill server, reload, confirm values/spill/formats survive) plus locale-persistence check — subsystem probes beyond run.sh.

Spot-checked formula outputs against known Excel results; caught YEARFRAC = 5.0055 vs expected 5.0 and corrected it — hand-grounded oracle checking, though informal (from Excel knowledge, not a LibreOffice corpus).

At close, relied on '131 dev tests pass' as headline signal; collab seq/broadcast, iterative calc, and goal-seek convergence were exercised only via the smoke suite, not independently verified — short of a systematic multi-subsystem harness.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well past the smoke suite: it wrote its own performance benchmarks against the stated ceilings, openpyxl/CSV round-trip tests, persistence/restart and locale probes, exercised error sentinels, and spot-checked function outputs against known Excel values (catching and fixing YEARFRAC), consistently using failures to drive fixes — matching anchor 8 closely. It falls short of 10 because the verification was ad-hoc python probes rather than a systematic harness, expected values came from the agent's own Excel knowledge rather than a real oracle tool, and several subsystems (collab, iterative calc, goal-seek, spill collisions) were only covered by the visible suite.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Verifies '195 functions registered' as a lump-sum count rather than tracking which functions per family are done/partial — coarse catalog tracking.
Consistently reconciles progress against live test-suite results ('78/80', '83', 'all 131 pass') after each fix — verification-grounded status, not just self-report.

Re-debugs the LET/LAMBDA bug over ~6 iterations, but each round advances the diagnosis (parser uppercasing, sed mismatch, quote chars) and resolves it — noticing the repeated failure and adjusting rather than looping blindly.
Explicit checklist of the required SPA data-testids with ✓ marks — a concrete done/remaining ledger for one subsystem.
Repeatedly enumerates likely hidden-test areas and detects its own coverage gaps (adds SUMPRODUCT/LARGE/SMALL at 88,105), showing active tracking of what's still outstanding beyond the smoke suite.
Final feature-family rollup listing every subsystem as complete — accurate end-state picture reconciled to what was built.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains an accurate picture of done-vs-remaining across the whole horizon and — crucially — reconciles it against verification results (test-pass counts) rather than mere self-report, while periodically enumerating outstanding risk areas and catching its own coverage gaps, which is well above anchor 5. However it never maintains a truly granular live ledger of the ~150-function catalog or endpoint families with explicit done/partial/not-started state (tracking is count-based and prose-enumerated), and it briefly re-debugged the same LET/LAMBDA issue several times before resolving it — falling short of the disciplined granular ledger and crisp thrash-detection described at anchor 8. This places it at a 6, between the checklist anchor (5) and the granular-ledger anchor (8).

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Detected contract-shape mismatch (POST /api/workbooks should return sheet-name list) from test failure and revised the endpoint rather than forcing the original shape.

VLOOKUP range_lookup=FALSE and ISERROR failures; agent reasoned explicitly about Excel's exact/approximate convention and reworked call dispatch to convert exceptions to error sentinels — an assumption-level fix, not a surface patch.
The ISERROR change crashed the server (mis-indented insertion); agent reacted to the hard crash and patched the malformed block — shows lower-anchor crash-reaction behavior mixed in.

Named-LAMBDA `triple(7)` returned #NAME?; agent diagnosed the true root cause (parser uppercasing function names so scope lookup missed) and reworked the parser to preserve original casing — root-assumption correction in the parse/eval model, then re-verified full suite.
Stripped openpyxl _xlfn. prefix and detected subtly-wrong YEARFRAC (5.0055 vs 5.0), diagnosing basis-dependence and fixing — recognizing subtly-wrong results, not just crashes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognized when a failure signaled a wrong underlying assumption — parser casing in the LAMBDA lookup, VLOOKUP range_lookup semantics, error-function dispatch, YEARFRAC basis, and a contract shape — and reworked the relevant design while re-running the suite each time, matching anchor 8. It stays below 10 because divergence was mostly detected post-hoc after building the full surface rather than caught early during incremental verification, and one correction introduced a regression crash rather than clean deliberate steering.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Built the entire function catalog breadth-first (195+ functions across math/stats/dist/financial/date/engineering/database/lookup/text families) in batched chunks before any deep edge-case work — securing broad coverage of common families first.
Implemented the full endpoint surface (fill/sort/filter/csv/names/validation/conditional-formats/settings/pivot/goal_seek/xlsx/websocket/SPA) as a breadth pass rather than perfecting one area.

Explicitly enumerated what the hidden suite likely grades (100k perf, persistence, playwright, ~200 hidden formula cases, OOXML round-trip) and used that to prioritize hardening — reasoning about graded return.

Consciously deferred the SPA rewrite ('skip SPA improvement... focus on more impactful items') because it already passed visible tests — a deliberate breadth-vs-depth reallocation away from low-marginal-yield work.
Added commonly-missing functions (SUMPRODUCT/LARGE/SMALL) while explicitly deciding niche ones (CHOOSECOLS/WRAPROWS) 'probably not needed' — timeboxing/deferring low-yield niches.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly reasoned about graded return: it secured broad working coverage across the entire function catalog and endpoint families before deep edge-case work (23-51), then repeatedly enumerated hidden-suite risk areas to steer hardening (86-90, 111) and consciously deferred low-yield work such as the SPA rewrite and niche functions (107, 111). This matches the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the reallocation was somewhat ad hoc ('build everything, then harden') rather than a continuously revisited allocation strategy driven by verification signals.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
